note: Constructed by the project team to demonstrate circuit figures in the no-API demo. These are not model output and not past-paper questions. Each loads as a v2 draft; the blind solve still has to run before approval.

drafts.label: Constructed: brightest of four circuits
drafts.description: Constructed example with four circuit diagrams. The server solves each circuit and confirms that only the keyed circuit has the brightest bulb.

draft.title: Batteries and bulbs in four circuits
draft.context: Mei Ling builds the four circuits shown. All the batteries are identical and all the bulbs are identical. Every bulb works and all the connections are secure.
draft.question: In which circuit does bulb P light up most brightly?

answer.explanation: Circuit B has two batteries in series and only one bulb, so the current through bulb P is the largest and P is the brightest. More batteries in series give a larger current; more bulbs in series give a smaller current.
steps: Count the batteries in series: B and D have two; A and C have one.
Count the bulbs in series: B and C have one; A and D have two.
B has more batteries than C and fewer bulbs than D, so bulb P in B has the largest current.

distractors.reason: Circuit A has one battery and two bulbs in series, so it has the smallest current of the four.
Circuit C has one battery and one bulb; the second battery in series in Circuit B makes the bulb brighter.
Circuit D has two batteries but also two bulbs in series, so bulb P is about as bright as in Circuit C, not as bright as in Circuit B.

mappings.evidence: Compares how the number of batteries in series and the number of bulbs in series change how brightly a bulb lights.
Reads four circuit diagrams to predict what each built circuit does.

design.reasoningTask: Combine two variables read from diagrams (batteries in series, bulbs in series) to find the brightest bulb.
requiredKnowledge: More batteries in series give a larger current.
More bulbs in series give a smaller current.
design.originalityRationale: Constructed by the project team to demonstrate the figure checker. It follows a common textbook comparison and makes no originality claim.

drafts.label: Constructed: bulbs with an open switch
drafts.description: Constructed example with a parallel branch and an open switch. The server solves the circuit and confirms that only the keyed option lists the bulbs that light.

draft.title: Which bulbs light with the switch open?
draft.context: Ravi sets up the circuit shown. All the bulbs are identical and work, and all the connections are secure. Switch S1 is open.
draft.question: Which bulbs light up?

answer.explanation: Bulbs A and B are in a closed circuit with the battery, so they light. The branch with bulb C is broken by the open switch S1, so no current flows through bulb C.
steps: Trace a closed path from the battery through bulb A.
After bulb A, the path through bulb B is closed, so A and B light.
The path through bulb C has the open switch S1, so C does not light.

distractors.reason: Bulb A is not alone in a closed path; the branch with bulb B completes the circuit too.
Bulb A is in the main loop, so it lights whenever any other bulb lights; bulb C is in the open branch.
Switch S1 is open, so no current flows through bulb C.

mappings.evidence: Decides which bulbs are in a closed circuit when a switch is open.
Reads a circuit diagram with a parallel branch and a switch.

design.reasoningTask: Trace closed paths in a diagram with a parallel branch and an open switch.
requiredKnowledge: A bulb lights only in a closed circuit.
An open switch breaks the path in its branch.
